user.title: Add a web data source
user.description: For the full visual experience, open **Web Data Assistant** in the sidebar now. You can also continue here using the standard Home Assistant setup flow.

data_description.source_name: A friendly name for this source, such as Carlow Weather or Electricity Prices.
data_description.source_type: Use JSON/API for structured responses, or Web page for visible content on an HTML page.

source.title: Connect to the source
source.description: Enter the source address. Web Data Assistant will fetch it now so you can choose the data you want from the real response.

data_description.headers: Optional request headers as a JSON object, such as an Authorization header with a bearer token.
data_description.payload: Optional raw request body. Usually only needed for POST requests.
data_description.verify_ssl: Keep enabled unless you intentionally connect to a source with a self-signed certificate.

json_mode.title: How do you want to use this JSON?
json_mode.description: Choose individual values for normal sensors, or retain the complete response as structured sensor attributes.

json_values.title: Choose JSON values
json_values.description: Web Data Assistant found {count} selectable values in the response. Choose one or more values to create as sensors.

json_full.title: Keep the full JSON response
json_full.description: This creates one sensor whose state is Loaded and stores the complete JSON response in its data attribute. This can be useful in templates and automations, but large or frequently changing responses can increase Recorder database usage.

data.confirm: I understand and want to keep the full response

scrape_search.title: Find the value on the page
scrape_search.description: Enter text that is currently visible on the page. Web Data Assistant will find the matching HTML element for you.

data_description.search_text: Use the value as it appears now, such as 14.6 °C, Open, or Carlow.

scrape_match.title: Choose the correct match
scrape_match.description: The text appears in {count} places. Choose the result whose surrounding content matches the value you want.

behaviour.title: Refresh and failure behaviour
behaviour.description: Choose how often this source updates and what its sensors should do if the website or API temporarily cannot be reached.

data.failure_mode: If the source cannot be reached

data_description.max_stale_minutes: Optional. When keeping the last value, mark it unavailable once the last successful update is older than this. Leave empty to keep it indefinitely.

error.cannot_connect: The source could not be reached or returned an error.
error.invalid_headers: Headers must be a valid JSON object.
error.no_json_values: The response was valid JSON, but no selectable scalar values were found.
error.text_not_found: That text could not be found in the fetched page. Check the value exactly as it currently appears.

init.title: Web Data Assistant settings
init.description: Adjust how often this source refreshes and how temporary source failures are handled.

data.failure_mode: If the source cannot be reached

data_description.max_stale_minutes: Optional. When keeping the last value, mark it unavailable once the retained value becomes older than this.
